items.comment: The `@param i` states a range precondition ('must be in the range from `0` until the length of the array') but never says what happens when it's violated. `a(i)` throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` for an out-of-range index, and this exact file already establishes the convention of documenting that with `@throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException if \`i < 0\` or \`length <= i\`` on `Array.apply`/`Array.update` (lines 836, 847). Adding the same `@throws` tag here would make the new doc consistent with the sibling convention in the same file.

Accurate explanation of the literal-type `false` trick used by the name-based extractor protocol. Slightly long as a single run-on sentence, but not misleading and not disruptive enough to require a change.
